In [[set theory]], the '''critical point''' of an [[elementary embedding]] of a [[transitive class]] into another transitive class is the smallest [[ordinal number|ordinal]] which is not mapped to itself.<ref>{{cite book|last=Jech|first=Thomas|author-link=Thomas Jech|title=Set Theory|publisher=Springer-Verlag| location=Berlin|year=2002|isbn=3-540-44085-2|pages=323}}</ref>

Suppose that ''j'':&nbsp;''N''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''M'' is an elementary embedding where ''N'' and ''M'' are transitive classes and ''j'' is definable in ''N'' by a formula of set theory with parameters from ''N.''  Then ''j'' must take ordinals to ordinals and ''j'' must be strictly increasing.  Also ''j''(ω)&nbsp;=&nbsp;ω.  If ''j''(''α'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;''α'' for all ''α''&nbsp;<&nbsp;''κ'' and ''j''(''κ'')&nbsp;>&nbsp;''κ,'' then ''κ'' is said to be the ''critical point'' of ''j.''

If ''N'' is ''[[Von Neumann universe|V]]'', then ''κ'' (the critical point of ''j'') is always a [[measurable cardinal]], i.e. an uncountable [[cardinal number]] ''κ'' such that there exists a ''κ''-complete, non-principal [[ultrafilter]] over ''κ.'' Specifically, one may take the filter to be {{{nnbsp}}A&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;κ&nbsp;| κ&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''j''(''A''){{nnbsp}}}, which defines a bijection between elementary embeddings and ultrafilters.<ref name=Neeman>{{cite book|chapter=Ultrafilters and large cardinals|first=Itay|last=Neeman|author-link=Itay Neeman|title=Ultrafilters across Mathematics|publisher=AMS|year=2010}}</ref>  Generally, there will be many other <''κ''-complete, non-principal ultrafilters over ''κ.'' However, ''j'' might be different from the [[ultrapower]]s arising from such filters.

If ''N'' and ''M'' are the same and ''j'' is the identity function on ''N,'' then ''j'' is called ''trivial.''  If the transitive class ''N'' is an [[inner model]] of [[ZFC]] and ''j'' has no critical point, i.e. every ordinal maps to itself, then ''j'' is trivial.<ref name=Neeman/>
